summary: The customary-practice context and coordination mhalxowa mmašyowa favor continuation/proceeding over filling a measure. The supplied record does not demonstrate a semantic extension of existing I 'geschtrichen voll machen'.
mm- and -wa do not by themselves establish II active Infectum-wa: a homonym, contact verb, contraction or different diathesis must remain open. No unattested base forms or meaning are published.

Read-only form lookup of mmašyowa returns mšy by consonantal compatibility (and myṣ only under relaxed diacritics); this is candidate retrieval, not lexical identification. Search mmaš supplies no matching proceeding example.
The existing I sense, Preterit example, Part. Pass. mašyo and unknown etymology remain unchanged. This is an unresolved reading candidate rather than a correction to them.
Jan English is machine translation [MT]. Its goes along, affairs run and conducts cannot identify a morphological stem by themselves.
All four Jan contexts differ semantically from the inherited fill-level-full entry. They add evidence for the proceeding family queried in round 1, but do not turn it into a subsense of filling.

Jan 3.56/1634 pairs kəmmašyo šane with komhalxina; 1644 has Mmašela ʕam i ʕito. These are additional course-of-affairs contexts comparable to round-1 mmašyowa with mhalxowa. Their subject/object and experiencer coding remain unresolved.
Bare maše at Jan 1.39/1719 occurs in a purpose clause whose referent is unclear. Jan 4.II/812 has ḥa and kmašele, possibly with an object suffix, but neither proves III or an Arabic causative loan.

Round 1 withheld a new stem and unattested base forms. Jan adds two plausible related shape families but does not securely decide homonymy, loan affiliation or diathesis; that decision remains unchanged. No examples are added to a misleading inherited sense or uncertain new box.
Identify the lemma, stem and diathesis of mmašyowa in JTM 1.5/50 from recording or speaker evidence. Does it mean proceed or be carried on, and is it a separate homonym from I fill-level-full?
Can a reliable standalone form establish whether a contact verb is involved? The edition's free German Alltag rendering does not settle this.
Identify lemma, homonym and stem for maše, kəmmašyo, Mmašela and kmašele from speakers or recordings. Are all one proceeding/management verb?
At Jan 1.39/1719 who or what proceeds in dəm maše? At 3.56/1634 is šane subject or object, and at 1644 what participant does -la encode?
Is kmašele at Jan 4.II/812 conduct/manage with an object suffix, or another construction? Supply standalone base forms before a new stem is published.
